xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-4640: Add scheduled conversations that run a prompt on a recurring schedule

plan.title: Add scheduled conversations that run a prompt on a recurring schedule
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

references.label: PAN-4657 (dashboard slice split out of this issue)
PAN-4639 (snooze and settle; #4657 depends on it)

metadata.sizeJustification: The plan touches exactly 25 files, but the subsystem count (11) is inflated by single-file entries that the lint counts as their own subsystem: package.json, bun.lock, and four separate doc files (features/conversations.mdx, docs/DASHBOARD-ARCHITECTURE.md, cli/overview.mdx, sync-sources/skills). The code spans src/lib (door, recurrence, resume cause), src/dashboard/server (routes, sweep), src/cli (verbs), drizzle (schema) and tests/unit (no-loss matrix). That backend slice is already the minimum shippable unit: the CLI is how an agent schedules itself, and the sweep is what fires it. The separable dashboard slice (dialog, badge, list event, inbox resurfacing) was split into sibling issue #4657.

narratives.Problem: Overdeck has no time-based trigger for a conversation. Recurring work lives inside a harness session's own wakeup or cron tools, which die with the process; src/lib/resume-contract.ts tells a resumed session to re-arm them itself. The t3code demo cited by the issue shows a thread that runs a stored prompt daily at 21:00, survives restarts, and resurfaces when it runs.
narratives.Proposal: Add a conversation_schedules table in overdeck.db with a door (src/lib/overdeck/conversation-schedules.ts), a recurrence module on croner 10.0.1 (5-field cron plus IANA zone, presets compiled to cron, 15-minute minimum spacing), REST routes under /api/conversations/:name/schedules, a dashboard-resident 60 s sweep (src/dashboard/server/services/conversation-schedule-service.ts, primary dashboard only) that claims each due schedule with a compare-and-set before firing (at-most-once, missed runs collapse to one), resumes an ended session with resume cause 'message' and then delivers the prompt through handleConversationMessage (follow_up for Pi, plain submit otherwise), records delivered/failed/skipped without retries, and pan conv schedule add|list|pause|resume|rm. The dashboard dialog, row badge and inbox resurfacing are split into #4657. Full detail: .pan/drafts/PAN-4640.md.
narratives.NonGoals:
- The dashboard Schedule dialog, the row next-run badge, the conversation-list nextScheduledRunAt field, the conversation.schedules_changed event, and clearing PAN-4639 snooze/settle state on a run (all in #4657)
- A new conversation per scheduled run; runs reuse the scheduled conversation
- Per-schedule model or effort; a run uses the conversation's current model and effort
- Cost or token caps beyond the 15-minute minimum spacing
- Retrying a failed run before its next occurrence
- Honoring the deacon pause toggle or the boot resume gate; scheduled runs follow the operator-message rule
- Schedules on agent conversations (agent-, planning-, specialist- prefixes) or Session Vault browse copies
- Seconds-level cron, 6- or 7-field patterns, @daily-style nicknames, and one-shot schedules
- Remote access-token scopes (route-scopes.ts) for the schedule routes
- Firing schedules from a peer dashboard or from the forked deacon child
- Growing src/lib/overdeck/conversations.ts by any line (it sits exactly at its allowlist cap)

autoDecisions.summary: Split the dashboard dialog, row badge, list-refresh event and inbox resurfacing into sibling issue #4657; this issue ships schema, door, recurrence, sweep, routes, CLI and docs.
autoDecisions.rationale: Resurfacing needs PAN-4639's snooze/settle columns, which are still being planned; the split lets this issue ship now, the CLI already covers the t3code self-scheduling flow, and the combined surface exceeds the 25-file finalize limit.

autoDecisions.summary: Run the sweep as a dashboard-resident service modeled on pull-request-sync-service.ts (primary dashboard only, boot +30 s, every 60 s), not as a deacon-lite patrol.
autoDecisions.rationale: deacon-lite runs in a forked child that reaches the dashboard only over internal HTTP and stops when the deacon is paused; resume and delivery live in the dashboard process and conversations are never gated. The 60 s cadence still meets the issue's 'within one deacon tick' criterion.

autoDecisions.summary: Claim each due schedule with a compare-and-set UPDATE that advances next_run_at to the next future occurrence before firing (at-most-once).
autoDecisions.rationale: A crash mid-fire then loses one run instead of duplicating a prompt, and computing the next occurrence from the wall clock collapses any number of missed runs into one.

autoDecisions.summary: Do not retry a failed run; record last_run_status 'failed' and the error and wait for the next occurrence.
autoDecisions.rationale: A daily schedule blocked by a permission prompt would otherwise retry every minute; the failure stays visible in pan conv schedule list.

autoDecisions.summary: Resume a conversation whose harness is not alive via handleConversationResume with a new optional resumeCause 'message', then deliver via handleConversationMessage.
autoDecisions.rationale: handleConversationMessage refuses ended sessions with 422 (the issue's claim that the message route resumes is not true), and the hardcoded cause would tell the agent the operator resumed it.

autoDecisions.summary: Deliver as follow_up only for Pi harnesses and as a plain submit for every other harness.
autoDecisions.rationale: pickDeliverAs defaults Pi to steer, and non-Pi harnesses refuse deliverAs follow_up with 422; Claude Code queues a plain submit behind a running turn.

autoDecisions.summary: Store a 5-field cron plus an IANA time zone; presets are CLI sugar; the default zone is the creating process's Intl zone stored on the row.
autoDecisions.rationale: One storage format keeps the sweep simple; Overdeck has no configured time-zone setting, and CLI and dashboard run on the same machine.

autoDecisions.summary: Use croner 10.0.1 pinned exactly in dependencies, always constructed with paused: true.
autoDecisions.rationale: Zero-dependency MIT library with correct DST handling (probed on 2026-11-01); 11.0.0 is only six days old; paused instances never arm timers in the server.

autoDecisions.summary: Reject recurrences whose occurrences are less than 15 minutes apart.
autoDecisions.rationale: Answers the issue's open cost-guard question without per-schedule budgets: an every-minute schedule on a frontier model would send 1,440 turns a day.

autoDecisions.summary: A scheduled run uses the conversation's current model and effort and reuses the same conversation.
autoDecisions.rationale: Answers the issue's two open questions with the t3code behavior and the smallest surface; both options can be added later without schema breakage.

autoDecisions.summary: Due schedules on archived conversations are advanced and recorded 'skipped', and resuming a paused schedule recomputes next_run_at from now.
autoDecisions.rationale: Neither unarchiving nor resuming should trigger a surprise catch-up run.

autoDecisions.summary: Prefix the delivered prompt with '[Scheduled run · schedule <id> · <cron> · <zone>]'.
autoDecisions.rationale: Tells the agent why the message arrived and prevents a stored prompt from being routed as a /pan composer command.

items.title: Add the croner-backed recurrence module with presets, validation and DST-correct next-run

expected_outputs: conversation-schedule-recurrence.test.ts passes including the three America/New_York DST fixtures

narrative.Action: Run `bun add croner@10.0.1 --exact` and create src/lib/overdeck/conversation-schedule-recurrence.ts exporting MIN_SCHEDULE_SPACING_MS, SchedulePreset, defaultScheduleTimeZone, isValidTimeZone, presetToCron, validateRecurrence and nextRunAfter exactly as PRD WI-1 specifies (exactly 5 fields; valid IANA zone via Intl.DateTimeFormat; croner parse; at least one future run; no two of the next 24 runs less than 15 minutes apart; croner always `paused: true`). Write the WI-1 tests with the cited DST fixtures; pass explicit Date values, no timers.

Add the dashboard sweep that fires due schedules

metadata.acJustification: Five unit-level criteria pin the firing semantics (collapse, lost claim, archived skip, no retry, resume-before-deliver, timer wiring); the sixth is the issue's end-to-end criterion that only a live dashboard can prove, kept on the item that owns the behavior so the test role verifies it here.

narrative.Action: Create src/dashboard/server/services/conversation-schedule-service.ts per PRD WI-5: runScheduleSweepOnce walks listDueSchedules sequentially, computes the next occurrence from the current clock, claims with claimScheduleRun before firing, records 'skipped' for archived conversations, and records 'delivered' or 'failed' (no retry). fireScheduledPrompt resolves the /clear chain head, resumes via handleConversationResume with resumeCause 'message' when conversationHarnessAlive is false, then calls handleConversationMessage with the '[Scheduled run · schedule <id> · <cron> · <zone>]' header and deliverAs 'follow_up' only for Pi harnesses. Start/stop copy the PR sync service (boot +30 s, 60 s, unref'd timers, non-overlap flag); wire them in src/dashboard/server/main.ts inside `if (!isPeerDashboard)` after the PR sync block and next to stopPullRequestSyncService. Tests inject every collaborator and use vi.useFakeTimers().
